text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Will the third stage of health reforms come at the end of the year?
- Bonn coalition divided over how sexual offenders should be punished
- Former member of once East German communist party, the SED, wants to be a judge at constitutional court
- More firms cut sick pay. IG Metall in Baden-Wuerttemberg threatens political response
- Economics Minister Guenther Rexrodt sees eastern Germany catching up despite various weaknesses
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- More firms decide to cut sick pay to 80 percent of gross earnings including Siemens, BASF, Hoechst and Schering as well as several banks. Volkswagen sticks to existing agreements
- EU stability pact does not have the bite that Finance Minister Theo Waigel wanted to give the Maastricht criteria
HANDELSBLATT
- Bonn ends reform of tax on heavy vehicles. EU commissioner Martin Bangemann threatens government with proceedings
- IG Metall says jobs take priority in a round of pay talks in the electronic industry
- Bertelsmann AG cancels plans to set up digital television
- Other firms follow Daimler-Benz's example and propose to cut sick pay
DIE WELT
- Patients should have more rights and doctors more accountable. Coalition approves plans for third stage of health reforms
- Discussion about how to punish sexual offenders
- Hamburg's regional government says Kruemmel nuclear power station is not been responsible for local leukaemia cases
- Globalisation increases rapidly. Importance of multinational firms grows according to report
- Tax payers federation want billion mark reduction in tax burden
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 2609760
